examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: CRC uses polynomial division over GF(2), where addition/subtraction is XOR. Append r zero bits for a degree-r generator, divide, and replace those zero bits with the r-bit remainder. The resulting codeword is divisible by the generator. Detection capability depends on generator factors and error patterns, not just checksum width.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A degree-4 CRC generator is used. How many remainder bits are appended?

**Answer: 4.** A polynomial remainder has degree less than 4 and is encoded in exactly four positions, including leading zeros. Thus four check bits are appended; the generator itself has five bits including its leading coefficient.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
CRC detects errors rather than correcting them. Zero remainder at the receiver can still occur for an undetectable error polynomial divisible by the generator.

CRC division uses XOR without carries or borrows.
